utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the local HVO group tell you when they saw that document?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: They read it and they told me that they couldn't sign it, that they would take it and check it with their commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they say where their commanders were?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: They told me they were in the Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any response back after the document had been taken to the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: Some two or three days later, I went back to see them, and they said they had been told not to sign anything. It wasn't a U.N.-produced document; it was something I produced myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the operational area, did you have an opportunity to visit the Ahmici area accompanying Colonel Stewart?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I accompanied Colonel Stewart everywhere, from Maglaj, Doboj, everywhere, and Ahmici. I accompanied him to Ahmici towards the end of the tour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this more than one visit or was it only one visit to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: No, I was there on at least three occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on one of the occasions that you visited Ahmici, do you recall finding any kind of evidence of bodies or destruction that you could describe?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: As we arrived in Ahmici, it was quite clear that the place was totally devastated, more than I had seen, and I travelled quite a bit of Central Bosnia. As we moved into the village and up past the mosque area, it wasn't too difficult to notice that a serious attack had taken place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see specifically that you can recall when you visited Ahmici the first time?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: The first time I saw, as we moved in from the main road, the mosque minaret blown down onto the main building. No sign of life at all. As we moved deeper in and up towards the sort of north of Ahmici, there was some fire still burning, some smoulders, but no one -- with some firing from the north, from the higher features to the north. We searched around that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find anything?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I was called to a building by a Lance Corporal Higginson because it was normal procedure for me to dismount in front of the Warrior vehicle and clear before them. We had been told that some atrocities had taken place. I thought we were in another area. We were in another area; we were in a place called Jelinak. So we got to Ahmici later in the afternoon. I believe that afternoon to be the day after the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that for certain or is that a guess on your part?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: That's a guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was keeping tracks of days and time a little bit difficult during this period of time for you and other members of the British battalion?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: It was very difficult. We were going from one village to another to try and -- to try and stop what was happening, basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Ahmici that day, I think you indicated that you had seen the mosque, and the spire had fallen down on the mosque.

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to examine the mosque for a period of time that day and come to some conclusions about what had caused the spire to fall?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I did have an occasion to go inside the building to investigate inside where I saw a number of unexploded missiles. I noticed that the minaret had been, in my opinion, it had been completely blown down using explosives rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher at this time to show the witness the following exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 161.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at Exhibit, what has been marked 161, which is a photograph placed next to you, and tell us what that depicts and perhaps you can tell us who took that photograph?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I took the photograph, and I took it because I hadn't seen that type of munitions before. To me it looked like some sort of stick-type grenade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: It was taken inside the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This would be the mosque with the minaret that was down?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other ordinance or explosive devices inside the mosque that day?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I saw another RPG-7 warhead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is an RPG-7 warhead?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: An RPG-7 rocket is a shoulder-fired anti-tank -- light anti-tank system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what the inside of the mosque looked like when you went in there?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: The mosque had been ransacked, basically. All windows smashed; just about everything in it torn apart, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned that you had seen the minaret of the mosque was, I think your words were "blown down." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I meant that in my opinion, charges were placed at the bottom of that minaret to blow it down in exactly the position that it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What led you to that view?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: As I mentioned, I travelled everywhere in Central Bosnia and witnessed -- or arrived in towns and cities shortly after attacks, and this was the first time I had seen a minaret completely down. Most of them, even in areas where heavy fighting, in the north of -- in the Tuzla area and places like that, they could take heavy hits and still stay up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I'll ask the usher to show the next photographic exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P-162.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Captain Stevens could you look at the photograph now marked 162 and tell us what that shows, and whether that helps illustrate your testimony that it is your view that the mosque minaret had been blown down by dynamite charges?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I can confirm this is a picture of that mosque, and you will see, if you look close to the base, it's difficult to see on the screen, but you'll see that this is reinforced with steel wires. It's a very thick structure. You would have to place charges against it to bring it down anyway. I believe it was brought down in exactly that position to cause further damage to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And had it been brought down in another way, would it have blocked the road in or out of Upper Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've talked about the mosque during your trip to Ahmici. Did you see anything else of interest during that first trip into Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: On the first -- as I mentioned earlier, on the first trip into Ahmici, we'd gone there because there were rumours of an atrocity committed. As we passed that mosque and moved further up into the village and up into what I've heard you refer to as Upper Ahmici, as we searched through the buildings to try and find some evidence of atrocity, I was called to a large structured building that had two bodies in the doorway, one that appeared to be a child and one that was of a man in the doorway. They had both been burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps to illustrate this a little better, if I could ask the usher to set up the blow-up of the village of Ahmici, and then ask the witness, with the pointer in front of him, to show the route that they took through the village that day, and where the house was where those bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I believe this large house to be -- this one here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is just your best estimate, you're not certain?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: It may have been further up here. It was on this side of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show us, perhaps, the route that you took that day to get to that part of Ahmici where you found those charred bodies?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: The route we took that day, we were travelling this way down the valley road, and we turned right in towards -- past the mosque and up this main route here. We drove as far as we could, but the armoured vehicles, it was very difficult, so we then dismounted and started to look around these houses here for signs of bodies and atrocities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this would be, just for purposes of the record, in an area that is known, I guess as Upper Ahmici, past the spot marked "Upper Mosque", would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: That would be, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say you found some burned bodies. Could you describe a little more what you found?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: We found -- on the steps of this house we found a small child's body, and in the hallway and in the doorway the body of an adult man. On further investigating around that building, in the cellar we found the bodies of another adult -- at least one other adult and a number of children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I could ask the usher to show the witness previously admitted Exhibits 17 and 22. Captain Stevens, this is previously admitted Exhibit 17. Could you tell us what that shows?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: This shows us the picture of the adult male in the hallway of his house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this one of the charred bodies that you had found on the day you visited to Ahmici, as you just indicated?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show Exhibit 22 now please? Thank you. And what does Exhibit 22 show?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: This shows the body of a child on the steps leading up into that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, are these the bodies that you found outside that house on that day?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go inside the house?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I didn't go into the upper level of the house, I went around the back into the cellar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see there?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I saw the bodies of a -- at least another male and several small children, two to three children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what conditions were these bodies?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: They were burnt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, while you were in Ahmici that day, have an opportunity to look around a little bit and observe things, in addition to what you've already described?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: Yeah. We arrived there in the afternoon and spent some time in this upper part when we found that particular house. It was getting dark. It was clear that there may be a risk of mines or any other booby-trap devices, so we quickly looked through the other buildings. And I went down into this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, pointing to an area, for purposes of the record, near the centre of the map where there's a big white space. Would that be accurate?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: That's right. I did spot someone down in this area with a -- someone moving around in there caught my eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is not a person with the British battalion?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: No. This was a person in half military uniform and half civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you approach this individual?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: Yeah. I basically went in sort of a wide half circle behind him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he carrying a weapon, this individual?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: He was carrying an AK-47.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to have some sort of conversation with this person?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: My recollections were that this person called himself Dragan, and he told me, by drawing in the dirt on the ground, that he'd killed 32 Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did he tell you this? How did he convey this information?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: "Muslim man," was how they spoke about the Muslim men. He made a hand across his throat and drew it into the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "hand across his throat"?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: A slashing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you take that to mean?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I took it that he was bragging to me that either then or in his past he'd killed 32 Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Just to be, I guess, absolutely clear as to where this person was, as best you can recall, I would ask the usher to provide the witness with the following exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P-163.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Captain Stevens, could you look at Exhibit 163 and see if you recognise that.

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I recognise this area as the-- can people see that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you use your pointer on the machine, I think it's easier for people to see on the television.

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: I recognise -- this area here is where I first saw this person moving around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps draw -- take one of those markers in front of you, an orange one might show up pretty well, and draw just a circle in the area where you recall talking to this individual? Do you recall anything else that he said to you that day, this person who called himself Dragan?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: No, I don't. I just recall that -- I just got the impression, and I really don't know why, that he lived somewhere close by here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the things you've already mentioned, did you see any other signs of either a battle or an attack, or of a -- anything else to indicate that -- what had gone on in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: There was a lot of expended cartridges. Generally 762, which is the AK ammunition, short ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a recollection of where these cartridges tended to be found?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: Generally around the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking about the houses, can you describe the condition of the houses in Ahmici that you saw when you arrived there the first time?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: What I saw was virtually the whole village burnt and sacked. To me it looked like a systematic sacking of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to draw any conclusions, as a professional soldier for 22 years in the British army, as to what, in fact, had happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, I've travelled with Colonel Stewart everywhere, to all the lines in various places in Central Bosnia, and seen some horrendous scenes at that time. This was the first time that I'd seen a village totally destroyed virtually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it your view, as a professional soldier, that what had happened in Ahmici was a battle, or was it your view, as a professional soldier, that, in fact, something else happened in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: In my opinion, it was definitely not a battle, it was an operation to remove the Muslim inhabitants of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, again, what led you to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: Charles Stevens
utterances.text: Houses still good structured, wealthy owners' houses still intact. As ballpark estimate, we -- any four-sided roof type building we regarded as Muslim, although that wasn't always generally true. But what we regarded a Muslim house was burnt or ransacked in that area, and the others weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the hour. I don't know if we're continuing past 5.00. I do have another area to get into.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Actually, I was wondering whether you had many more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: I have another area to get into that will involve a videotape and some photographs, questions that may take a little time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So we'll adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.30 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
